decisions.rationale: In the opening sentence, 'skin tumour' refers to the single tumour type the abstract studies (pilomatricoma), so it is annotated as a specific disease rather than a broad family.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 - Specific Disease vs Disease Class

decisions.rationale: 'cancer' is used generically for a family of many distinct malignant diseases, so it is a Disease Class. The term 'cancer' is retained by the guidelines.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 - Disease Class; What NOT to Annotate §4 (cancer is retained)

decisions.rationale: 'colon cancers' names one definable disease (colon cancer) without further subcategorisation, and it is the head noun of the phrase, so it is not a modifier.
'adenomatous polyposis coli' names the APC gene product, a protein, which is described as 'a protein required for ubiquitin-mediated degradation'. It is not used as a disease mention here.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (only disease mentions are annotated); What NOT to Annotate §1 (non-disease entities)

decisions.rationale: 'APC' is the abbreviation of the protein/gene product adenomatous polyposis coli, not a disease mention in this context.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (only disease mentions are annotated); What NOT to Annotate §1 (non-disease entities)

decisions.rationale: 'colon and some other cancers' is a contiguous string covering two or more separate disease mentions (colon cancer and other cancers), so it is annotated as a single Composite Mention.
'skin tumours' is a plural general category that includes pilomatricomas as one member, so it is a family of diseases rather than one specific disease.
'pilomatricomas' is a named, specific tumour entity with a single definition.
'human pilomatricomas' refers to the specific named tumour entity pilomatricoma; the organism modifier 'human' is excluded from the mention span.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 - Specific Disease; What NOT to Annotate §1 (organism names excluded)

decisions.rationale: 'this common human skin tumour' refers back to the pilomatricoma studied in the abstract, so it denotes one specific disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 - Specific Disease; §4 (duplicate mentions annotated)

decisions.rationale: 'tumour' is used as a modifier of the noun 'cells' in 'dividing tumour cells', so it is annotated as a Modifier.
'pilomatricomas' is again the named specific tumour entity, here as the subject of the derivation claim.
'these tumours' is a coreferent mention of pilomatricomas in the same context, so it denotes that specific disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 - Specific Disease; §4 (duplicate mentions annotated)

decisions.rationale: 'all other human tumours examined thus far' is a generic reference to a broad family of tumour types, so it is a Disease Class.
'tumorigenesis' refers to the biological process of tumour formation, not to a disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate §5 - biological processes
